answer: In PoA, each identity posts bonded collateral in an escrow, while equivocation proofs link signatures and slash every implicated bond. For k coordinated identities, correlated equivocation carries a quadratic penalty, O(k^2), rather than k independent fines; asymmetric depreciation then applies an exponential multiplier to aggregate capital loss upon detection. Thus, a sybil swarm using falcon, lagoon, and velvet aliases becomes economically prohibitive.
